newsitem.title: USA: BASKETBALL-K.C. JONES NAMED COACH OF WOMEN'S PRO BLIZZARD TEAM.
newsitem.headline: BASKETBALL-K.C. JONES NAMED COACH OF WOMEN'S PRO BLIZZARD TEAM.

text.p: Basketball Hall of Famer K.C. Jones took on a new challenge Tuesday when he officially became head coach of the New England Blizzard of the women's American Basketball League.
Jones, an assistant this past season with the Boston Celtics, has been a part of 12 NBA championship teams -- eight as a player, two as a head coach and two as an assistant.

"I'm very excited about this opportunity," said Jones, who turns 65 later this month. "I've had the chance to coach young girls and young women in my camps for many years and have always been impressed by how enthusiastic and coachable they are."
After a nine-year playing career with Boston (1958-67) that featured NBA titles from 1959-66, Jones began his coaching career at the college level with Brandeis and Harvard.

He returned to the NBA in 1971 as an assistant with the Los Angeles Lakers, who won a then-NBA record 69 games that season and the NBA title. Jones' first pro head coaching job came in 1972 with the ABA's San Diego Conquistadors.

The next season, he took over the NBA's Bullets and held the job for three years before serving as an assistant with Milwaukee and Boston. Jones was elevated to head coach of the Celtics in 1983 and compiled a 308-102 record in five seasons with two NBA championships.
Jones, who was elected to the Basketball Hall of Fame in 1988, later coached the Seattle SuperSonics before joining the coaching staff of the Detroit Pistons in 1994.
Overall, Jones owns a 522-252 regular-season mark in 10 years in the NBA and an 81-57 playoff record.

"Last week, I went to Hartford to meet with the staff and some of the players of the New England Blizzard," Jones said. "I was very impressed with the general manager (Pam Batalis), and the players were awesome.
"I'm very anxious to get started and to build a championship team in New England."
